item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Transition-Metal-Oxygen Covalency Controls Ligand-Hole Stability in Li-Rich Cathode
item.description: arXiv:2610.20837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lithium-rich cathodes boast a large specific capacity due to the presence of excess lithium per transition metal. However, making use of that excess Li drives the cathodes to unusually high formal oxidation states, often triggering unwanted side reactions, typically signaled by gas release and commonly associated with oxygen oxidation. By varying the transition metal (TM) chemistry in Li-rich materials, cyclability can vary drastically, with some materials suffering rapid capacity fade while others are able to maintain large and stable voltage windows. Such observations indicate a crucial role for both TM and O activities, but the details remain elusive. Here, we model core-level spectroscopy to understand differences in the charge compensation mechanism between different Li2MO3 (M = Mn, Ru, Ir) cathode materials. We find that ligand holes are important throughout the series, but their stability depends strongly on the transition-metal-oxygen electronic structure. In Li2MnO3, the ground state is already strongly negative-charge-transfer-like, so further delithiation rapidly increases ligand-hole character and promotes instability. Moving from Mn to Ru and Ir increases TM-O hybridization while reducing the tendency toward an extreme negative-charge-transfer state, allowing additional holes to remain delocalized over the covalent TM-O network over a wider range of charge. These results identify TM-O covalency, rather than the absence of oxygen-hole character, as a key factor controlling reversible high-valent redox and suggest a route for stabilizing high-energy-density cathodes without invoking reversible molecular oxygen formation.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Fisher information analysis of a Langevin System with Thermal and Athermal Noise
item.description: arXiv:2610.20963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fisher Information (FI) has proven to be a useful tool for estimating the parameters of a system when only statistical data are available. We apply this method to a system of Langevin equations analogous to the Brownian Gyrator, in which the coupling parameter $b$ and the athermal noise strength $D$ are treated as unknown quantities. Using the FI, we discuss the estimation of the coupling parameter between the degrees of freedom and the quantity $D$ associated with the external noise effects. We find that the diagonal components of the FI exhibit nontrivial behavior, whereas the off-diagonal components display a monotonic dependence on the parameters of interest. This distinction may contribute to an accurate estimation of $b$ and $D$.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Broadband radio-frequency TEM specimen holders for in situ biasing excitation and 100-ps-scale electron beam control
item.description: arXiv:2610.21275v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Broadband electrical excitation inside a transmission electron microscope (TEM) is required to investigate electrically driven nanodevices at their actual operating frequencies and to develop fully electrical time-resolved experiments at a sub-nanosecond range. Here, we report the performances of homemade two- and four-channel radio-frequency (RF) TEM specimen holders based on a hybrid architecture combining coaxial transmission lines with miniaturized impedance-controlled printed circuit boards (PCB). Removable mechanical contacts provide direct electrical connection to interchangeable TEM chips without wire bonding. Vector network analyzer measurements demonstrate broadband transmission through the complete electrical path up to the specimen. With a representative TEM chip, the two-channel holder exhibits a -3 dB bandwidth of 7.9 GHz, while insertion losses remain below 12 dB up to 18 GHz. The same RF holder architecture was used to drive a miniaturized electrostatic electron-beam deflector. The measured temporal response indicates that the holder deflector assembly remains compatible with electrical pulse durations approaching 100 ps, with the shortest accessible times presently limited by the available waveform generator. High-resolution TEM imaging with a 200 ps probe window does not show detectable degradation of spatial resolution, while off-axis electron holography is successfully performed for probe durations down to 0.5 ns under conditions representative of operando measurements. These results establish a versatile broadband platform combining GHz electrical excitation and sub-nanosecond electron-beam control. The dual-stage configuration of our Hitachi HF3300 microscope further provides the basis for a future fully electrical pump-probe TEM approach using independently driven RF holders for specimen excitation and electron-probe control.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Dynamical phase transition for a logarithm observable in chaotic systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.21288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the full distribution $P_N(A)$ of the dynamical observable $A = - \sum_{i=1}^N \ln x_i$ where $x_1, \dots, x_N$ is a sequence generated by a chaotic map $f(x)$ via $x_{n+1} = f(x_n)$. We study the particular cases where $f(x)$ is the doubling, tent or logistic map, and focus on the limit $N \gg 1$. Typical fluctuations of $A$ are Gaussian with mean $\left\langle A\right\rangle$ and variance which are both of order $\sim N$. We find that the left tail of the distribution ($A < \left\langle A\right\rangle$) scales as $P_{N}(A) \sim e^{-NI(A/N)}$, and calculate the rate function $I(a)$ which depends on the map $f(x)$. Interestingly, we find that the right tail of the distribution ($A > \left\langle A\right\rangle$) follows an anomalous scaling: $P_{N}(A) \sim e^{-N^{1/3} F((A-\left\langle A\right\rangle) / N^{2/3})}$. The large-deviation function $F(y)$ has a universal form for the three maps, differing only in the scaling constants. At a critical value $y=y_c$, it exhibits a corner singularity which has the character of a condensation transition. The transition separates between a subcritical phase $0< yy_c$ in which a small fraction of the $x_i$'s give a macroscopic contribution to the fluctuation. Despite this anomalous behavior of the right tail, we find that the cumulants of the distribution $P_N(A)$ grow linearly with $N$ at large $N$, and calculate the associated coefficients.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Pairing-channel reconstruction by Ising spin-orbit coupling in a multiorbital triangular-lattice model
item.description: arXiv:2610.21369v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ising spin-orbit coupling (SOC) is widely known for locking electronic spins and protecting superconductivity against in-plane paramagnetic pair breaking. Here we show that, in a correlated multiorbital system, Ising SOC can play a qualitatively different role: it reconstructs the hierarchy of spin-fluctuation-mediated pairing channels by reshaping the low-energy Fermi surfaces, orbital-spin coherence factors, and momentum-resolved scattering phase space. We study a noncentrosymmetric two-orbital triangular-lattice model with Rashba SOC, Ising SOC, and onsite SOC. We solve the pairing problem within a multiorbital random-phase-approximation framework. In the single-orbital limit, an $E$-representation state with a dominant $S_z=0$ component emerges only at relatively strong Ising SOC. Orbital degrees of freedom facilitate the stabilization of this pairing state at a smaller nominal Ising SOC strength and generate a broad competition between $E$ and $A_1$ pairing channels. The $E$ state can maintain the same $S_z=0$ triplet character, whereas the $A_1$ state becomes a fully gapped sign-changing $\splusminus$ superconductor. The latter also realizes a topologically nontrivial phase in the time-reversal-invariant weak-pairing regime, with a nonzero $\mathbb{Z}_2$ index, Wilson-loop spectral flow, and boundary modes. Its topology is not carried by a single orbital pairing component, but emerges cooperatively from the dominant intra- and inter-orbital pairing components. These results establish a microscopic route by which Ising SOC and orbital hybridization can reconstruct interaction-driven superconductivity, producing both Ising-triplet and topological singlet-dominated phases in correlated non-centrosymmetric systems.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Edge state reconstruction in proximitized graphene and its probe using RKKY interaction
item.description: arXiv:2610.21416v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Proximity induced spin-orbit coupling (SOC) in graphene emerges when it is placed on a substrate, breaking sublattice symmetry and giving rise to staggered intrinsic SOC together with Rashba spin-orbit coupling. In zigzag graphene nanoribbons, this staggered SOC produces pseudohelical edge states exhibiting sublattice-locked rather than spin-locked helicity. We investigate the effect of a finite on-site potential, restricted to the edges of the ribbon, on these edge states. We find the inter-valley edge states undergo reconstruction and become purely intra-valley, exhibiting both spin and valley polarization. The charge conductance calculations fail to capture this reconstruction, since the number of transmitted channels remains unchanged. We show that the Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) magnetic exchange interaction, between two magnetic impurities situated on the ribbon edge can be used to probe the shifted band dispersion, for both the uniform and staggered spin-orbit coupling. In the presence of strong intrinsic and Rashba SOC, the RKKY interaction becomes fully anisotropic. Both sublattice staggering and edge potential-induced reconstruction lead to distinct features in the RKKY interaction. We show that the RKKY interaction terms acquire faster oscillations as a function of the spatial separation between two magnetic impurities, in response to the edge state reconstruction, establishing it as an effective probe of the edge states. Additionally, the significant mismatch in the amplitudes of the DM term corresponding to the uniform and staggered SOC, can also act as a probe of the type of SOC.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Non-equilibrium Muon Dynamics Imitating Fractional Spin Excitations in a Quantum Spin Chain
item.description: arXiv:2610.21523v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fractional spin excitations in low-dimensional and frustrated magnets are commonly associated with sporadic spin fluctuations, as observed in quantum spin liquids, spin ices, and other complex magnetic states. In this study, we investigate the spin dynamics in the amplitude-modulated magnetic ground state of AgCuVO$_4$, a spin-1/2 chain compound with competing intrachain interactions, by muon spectroscopy. Our data reveal a Gaussian decay of muon polarization that remains remarkably resilient against applied magnetic fields---a behavior often interpreted as evidence of emergent sporadic spin dynamics. However, density functional theory calculations of muon stopping sites and their quadrupolar level-crossing resonance spectra suggest an alternative mechanism: a two-state model where the muon randomly hops between two nearby sites, eventually equilibrating across both on a microsecond timescale via quantum delocalization. These findings provide a microscopic explanation for the field-resilient muon polarization and indicate that such behavior may not always stem from intrinsic spin fluctuations, but can also arise from non-equilibrium muon dynamics.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Finite-size geometric crossover toward fragmentation of the potential energy shell in the quantum random energy model
item.description: arXiv:2610.21631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The quantum random energy model (QREM) is a paradigmatic model for studying delocalization-localization transitions at finite energy density in Fock space. In the computational basis, its diagonal energies are independent Gaussian random variables, in contrast to the correlated energies of local interacting models such as the disordered XXZ chain. In this work, we construct a potential energy shell associated with a basis state, defined through its energy variance, and investigate its connectivity on the Fock-space hypercube. As the transverse field is varied, this energy-selected subgraph undergoes a finite-size geometric crossover between fully connected and fragmented regimes. Furthermore, we observe a correlation between the shell connectivity and the finite-size fractal dimension of the eigenstates, as extracted from the participation entropy. For the QREM, the statistical independence of the diagonal energies allows the shell connectivity to be analyzed as an effective independent site percolation problem on the hypercube, with its crossover scale estimated within a one-hop approximation. At finite energy density, this estimate gives a nonmonotonic dependence of the crossover scale on system size $L$: increasing $L$ initially favors connectivity, while beyond an energy-dependent scale $L^*(\varepsilon)$ the trend reverses towards fragmentation.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Defect Candidates for Single-Photon Emission in Monolayer GaS and GaSe
item.description: arXiv:2610.21670v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the spin-resolved electronic structure of native vacancies and substitutional defects in monolayer GaS and GaSe using an anisotropic screened-exchange functional developed for two-dimensional material systems. By combining an energy-based classification of defect-associated states with spatially resolved projections and partial charge densities, we examine how these defects modify the in-gap electronic structure and assess their relevance for defect-based single-photon emission. The results identify gallium vacancies, particularly in GaS, as candidates single-photon emitters.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Coexistence of Altermagnetic and Compensated Ferrimagnetic Motifs in a Noncollinear Multiferroic
item.description: arXiv:2610.21770v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Collinear compensated magnets with nonrelativistic spin splitting comprise altermagnets (ALMs), whose rotation- or mirror-related opposite-spin sublattices produce momentum-selective splitting that vanishes at $\Gamma$, and compensated ferrimagnets (CFIMs), whose symmetry-inequivalent sublattices allow splitting throughout the Brillouin zone, including at $\Gamma$. Here, we show that the coplanar noncollinear magnetic state of multiferroic boracite Ni$_3$B$_7$O$_{13}$Cl hosts both motifs on distinct Ni sublattices in real space. The electronic structure and spin texture exhibit coexisting $d$-wave-like and $s$-wave-like spin-polarization components associated with the ALM and CFIM motifs, respectively. Opposite ferroelectric states exhibit reversed band-resolved spin polarizations, indicating magnetoelectric coupling, and sign reversals of linear shift and circular injection currents.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Localization induced by Sinai disorder in mass-exchange models
item.description: arXiv:2610.21777v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a conservative continuous-mass-exchange model with quenched disorder in the splitting laws on the bonds of a finite segment. Although the dynamics is generically irreversible, its stationary mean mass profile remarkably turns out to be exactly solvable through an associated birth-and-death chain and has a Gibbs representation in terms of a simple random-walk potential. If $N$ is the number of bonds and $\beta$ measures the strength of disorder, the parameter $\beta\sqrt N$ separates an asymptotically flat profile, a Brownian crossover, and a profile localized near the global minimum. We characterize the fluctuations of macroscopic masses and identify arcsine laws for the localization centre, the competition between left and right valleys, and the disorder-averaged mass measure. Furthermore, for the extremal masses, we discuss the emergent limiting random variable in terms of the literature linking finite RW paths seen from its minimum to infinite-horizon walks conditioned to stay positive. Finally, in proximity of the localization transition point $\beta=0$, we show that the inverse participation ratio for the extremal masses give rises to a scaling with decay of order $k^{-3/2}$ consistent with the scaling limit of the latter conditioned walk. In the same limit, the inverse participation ratio shows a scaling form.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Extended strange metal and superconductivity in partially filled moir\'e Hubbard bands
item.description: arXiv:2610.22307v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Moir\'e semiconductors provide a physical realization of the Hubbard model. Bandwidth-tuned Mott transitions and complex phase diagrams mimicking those of high-temperature superconductors have been demonstrated near a weak Mott insulating state at half-band-filling. The platform also provides an opportunity to explore the physics of a partially filled Hubbard band at doping densities far away from the Mott insulator, a regime that has remained largely unexplored. Here we report the emergence of an extended strange metal (ESM), in both doping density and twist angle, in a partially filled Hubbard band of twisted bilayer WSe2. The ESM is in the clean limit, persists down to 100mK, and spans over multiple symmetry-breaking ground states; it also appears only at small twist angles, where electronic correlations are strong. These observations distinguish the state from the reported strange metals associated with quantum criticality and favor the viewpoint that it is an intrinsic state of matter. We also report the observation of a new superconducting dome being developed from the ESM but far away from both the Mott insulating state and the van Hove singularity of the material. Our work opens the door to exploring the new regime of partially filled Hubbard bands in the clean limit.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Second-Order Homogenization of Particulate Elastomeric Composites for Structural-Scale Damage Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2610.20624v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Damage prediction in particulate elastomeric composites is challenging due to the strong material heterogeneity, nearly incompressible behavior of the matrix, and the presence of localized stress concentrations arising from matrix-inclusion interactions. In the present work, a computational framework is developed for damage propagation analysis of particulate elastomeric composite structures. The effective constitutive response of the heterogeneous material is first determined using the second-order homogenization method. The resulting homogenized response is subsequently used to identify equivalent hyperelastic material parameters for structural simulations. A three-parameter isotropic damage model is incorporated to capture damage-induced softening. A mixed displacement-pressure finite element formulation, is used to alleviate volumetric locking associated with nearly incompressible property of elastomers. The proposed framework is validated through full-scale simulations and homogenized response involving composites with varying inclusion volume fractions. Numerical investigations demonstrate that the homogenized models is able to reproduce the global force-displacement response within 2% error and damage evolution characteristics of the heterogeneous composites while significantly reducing the computational cost.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Crystallization of the undertile
item.description: arXiv:2610.20663v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We classify all periodic tilings with a monotile known as $\mathbf{R1}$ and called here the undertile, which underlies several aperiodic monotiles such as the Taylor-Socolar one. The classification is done using deflation, through a study of fracture lines between zones where deflation can be performed. A full classification of fracture patterns is given, that also applies to non-periodic tilings with the undertile. This can be used to reprove non-periodicity of some existing monotiles based on the undertile.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Quantum instanton approach to metastable collective spin systems: Numerical implementation and applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.21684v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Driven-dissipative collective spin systems can host several long-lived metastable states; rare switching between them governs slow relaxation and first-order dissipative phase transitions associated with changes in the dominant stationary state. In the companion Letter [arXiv:2604.15091], we introduced a quantum instanton framework based on exact quasiprobability dynamics to describe this switching and illustrated it with a minimal model possessing a simplifying symmetry. Here we develop its numerical implementation, combining collocation and shooting methods, and apply it to two microscopically motivated systems: the Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick model with purely collective dissipation and the cooperative resonance fluorescence with collective and local dissipation. By determining the leading exponential scaling of switching rates between metastable attractors, we predict the stationary magnetization, the first-order dissipative phase-transition point, and the exponential scaling of slow relaxation rates. These predictions agree with quantum master-equation calculations and an exact analytical result for the second model without dephasing. We also examine how the choice of quasiprobability representation affects numerical convergence and find that the alternative semiclassical Wigner approach, based on Gaussian truncation, has varying accuracy across models and parameter regimes. These results substantiate the framework's applicability to experimentally relevant collective spin systems with both collective and local dissipation.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Density and shape govern the dynamical self-organization of active matter on a closed surface
item.description: arXiv:2603.23735v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Morphogenesis emerges from dynamic feedback among geometry, mechanics, and chemistry; however, disentangling these contributions in living systems remains challenging. Here, we focus on the interplay between geometry and mechanics by developing a minimal in vitro model in which purified microtubules and kinesin motor clusters self-organize into a two-dimensional active nematic cortex at the surface of spherical water-in-oil droplets. The spherical geometry enforces a total topological charge of +2, here realized by four +1/2 defects whose trajectories reveal robust, self-sustained oscillations. Using full-surface reconstructions, we show that the collective dynamics of the defects lead to a periodic switching between planar and tetrahedral arrangements through alternating coiling and hemisphere-crossing phases. By tuning microtubule density, the system spans a continuum from a classic defect-dominated active nematic to a regime resembling an extensile filament confined to a curved surface, where low density is associated with increased trajectory variability and direction reversals. Geometric perturbations introduced through controlled squeezing redistribute curvature and induce the nucleation of additional defects, thereby reorganizing the entire topological landscape while preserving total charge. Together, these results show that periodic morphogenetic-like cycles, defect topology, and material organization can arise solely from the interplay of activity, density, and curvature. This reconstituted system provides a versatile platform for elucidating the coupling between mechanics and geometry underlying shape formation in active biological matter.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Bulk-dissociated topological bands without spin-orbit coupling in hetero-dimensional superconducting metamaterials
item.description: arXiv:2604.08675v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Topological superconductors (TSCs) in superconducting hybrid heterostructures, which integrate superconducting and non-superconducting materials, have been intensely investigated with the hope of discovering exotic non-Abelian anyons for fault-tolerant quantum computing. In this effort, a challenge for hybrid superconducting systems is controlling hybridization, which is often a balance between enhancing the superconducting proximity effect at the cost of suppressing desirable electronic properties such as strong spin-orbit interactions. Hence, discovering hybrid superconducting systems with topological properties controlled and enhanced by material geometry design without spin-orbit interactions would be intriguing to explore. In this work, we theoretically study a square superconducting network decorated with spin-polarized magnetic adatoms. We find that localized Yu-Shiba-Rusinov bound states at magnetic adatom sites collectively form a weak topological superconducting phase despite the absence of spin-orbit interactions. We then demonstrate that by tuning the Fermi energy of the network, the system can transition from a weak TSC phase to a bulk-dissociated TSC phase where the edge state bands separate from the bulk, giving rise to unexpected features such as nodal lines and co-existing bulk-dissociated edge and corner modes. Moreover, our findings highlight how hetero-dimensional superconducting metamaterials can serve as a useful template for controlling the coupling and dissociation between electronic degrees of freedom of different dimensionalities.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Critical quench dynamics of Wegner's $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge model: a geometric perspective
item.description: arXiv:2605.15841v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Wegner's $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge model is the earliest formulation of pure lattice gauge theory and predicts the topological nature of the confinement-deconfinement transition. In three dimensions ($D=3$), the equilibrium critical behavior of the model is understood in terms of geometrically defined objects, namely loop excitations and Fortuin-Kasteleyn (FK) clusters. This work investigates the critical quench dynamics of this model from a geometric perspective, following quenches from both a high-temperature percolation phase and the zero-temperature ground state. Using time-dependent finite-size scaling analysis, we find that the critical non-equilibrium relaxation of the percolation order parameter is governed by a dynamical exponent $z_{\rm p} \simeq 2.6$, consistent with that associated with the energy density, $z_{\rm c}$. Importantly, the value of $z_{\rm p}$ is robust with respect to the initial quench condition and the choice of geometrical objects. Furthermore, we provide a detailed characterization of the kinetics of different geometrical objects during the evolution from the percolation phase. Notably, we observe that the quench dynamics obeys dynamic scaling in terms of a growing lengthscale, $\xi_{\rm p}(t) \sim t^{1/z_{\rm p}}$, despite the absence of a local order parameter.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] A Functorial Theory of Defects in Abelian Chern-Simons Theory
item.description: arXiv:2609.21414v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent work has constructed Abelian Chern-Simons theories as categorical TQFTs, allowing us to naturally incorporate categorical defects and construct defect extensions of Abelian Chern-Simons TQFTs. We first identify the Turaev-Viro realizations of Abelian Chern-Simons theory in the center and doubled pointed modular cases, clarifying the distinction between single bulk realizations and canonical doubled ones. Then we obtain Turaev-Viro partition functions in terms of Reidemeister-torsion densities. Alternatively, the Alterfold construction supplies the associated topological boundaries, domain walls, and condensation sectors, establishing an explicit Alterfold/Chern-Simons dictionary. We show that the finite quadratic module is the invariant controlling the bulk theory, its topological symmetries, orientation-reversal invariance, and defects. We further show that multicomponent Abelian BF theory arises as the extended TQFT of an off-diagonal Abelian Chern-Simons theory, placing it naturally within the same extended framework. Finally, we demonstrate that recently proposed Abelian Chern-Simons dualities do not define a genuine TQFT duality. These results provide a concrete model for defects in Abelian topological orders and suggest a route toward the non-Abelian case.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Spread Complexity for Local Operator Quenches with Conserved Momentum
item.description: arXiv:2609.31867v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study a family of locally excited states in two-dimensional conformal field theories in different setups, defined on the plane, on the cylinder, or at finite temperature. These states are constructed by assigning independent chiral and anti-chiral regulators to a local primary operator, leading to excitations carrying net momentum. We analytically calculate the first few Lanczos coefficients and the early time behaviour of the spread complexity associated with these states. Then, using numerical methods, we obtain the coefficients reaching larger Krylov indices and find the associated spread complexity for a longer range of time evolution. We also compare the rate of change of the resulting spread complexity with the proposed holographic dual quantity, related to the proper momentum of an infalling particle in the dual bulk, but we observe a mismatch.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs.AR updates on arXiv.org] Helix: A Unified Programmable Accelerator for Diverse Krylov Subspace Solvers
item.description: arXiv:2610.21096v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Domain-specific accelerators deliver high performance and energy efficiency through specialization but often lack support for extensible algorithm families. Existing FPGA accelerators for Krylov subspace methods, which iteratively solve sparse linear systems, typically support a single solver or require separate hardware configurations. Helix follows a systematic algorithm-family design methodology that first abstracts common computational primitives from diverse Krylov solvers and builds the architecture around efficient, programmable primitive kernels. Helix then introduces programmable datapaths to coordinate these primitives. Its architecture decouples hardware implementation from solver-specific execution, enabling HBM reuse and zero solver-switching latency. Finally, Helix provides a DSL compiler that efficiently maps different solvers onto the architecture while optimizing vector-operation performance for each solver. We prototype Helix on a Xilinx Alveo U55C FPGA and evaluate Helix's practicality and performance by using it to compile and execute eight solvers. Helix achieves up to 7.91x and 1.16x speedups over Xilinx XcgSolver and the state-of-the-art FPGA accelerator Callipepla, respectively, both of which support only JPCG. Across the eight solvers, Helix sustains 47.5% - 96.9% of the throughput of an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPU while delivering 2.29x - 4.66x higher energy efficiency and 1.89x - 3.85x higher throughput per unit peak memory bandwidth. The programmable components incur 0.25% - 0.57% execution-time overhead and 4.7% LUT and 4.0% FF overhead, demonstrating negligible overhead for programmability.
item.author: cs.AR updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs.AR updates on arXiv.org] PSA: A Pruning-Friendly Sparse-Aware Accelerator for Efficient Sparse Convolution in SNNs
item.description: arXiv:2610.21313v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) are promising for energy-efficient artificial intelligence due to their event-driven sparse computation, and neuron pruning can further reduce redundant operations. However, in practical hardware accelerators, spike sparsity and pruning-induced sparsity produce highly irregular sparse workloads that are difficult to execute efficiently. Existing approaches do not jointly support sparse-input execution, low-overhead sparse convolution lowering and pruning-friendly execution. This paper presents PSA, a Pruning-friendly Sparse-aware Accelerator for efficient sparse convolution in SNNs. PSA features a Sparse-Aware Merge-Accumulation (SAMA) dataflow that aligns sparse spike indices and converts irregular activations into continuous computation streams for efficient sparse convolution execution. It further introduces a Sparse Implicit Group-wise im2col (SIG-im2col) convolution lowering mechanism that converts sparse convolution into SpMM on-chip with low mapping cost and memory overhead. In addition, PSA integrates a lightweight pruning-friendly gating mechanism to directly support pruned SNNs. Results on ResNet-18/CIFAR-10 show that PSA achieves a 4.45x improvement in energy efficiency and an 18.52x reduction in energy-delay product (EDP) over the dense baseline.
item.author: cs.AR updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs.AR updates on arXiv.org] Minimum RISC-V: Maximum FPGA Efficiency
item.description: arXiv:2610.21552v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: RISC-V processors are now widely available for FPGAs, with most FPGA vendors replacing their proprietary soft-CPU architectures with this instruction-set architecture (ISA). Although contemporary FPGAs are increasingly resource- and feature-rich, a soft processor system---including memory---often occupies a disproportionately large footprint and delivers only modest performance relative to the potential of the target device. In this work we first design a lightweight but deeply pipelined RISC-V core that can run above 700 MHz in a mid-range device and that is capable of retiring one instruction per clock under ideal conditions. We then develop and demonstrate a new optimization method that compiles the final application binary and a specialized processor instance contemporaneously. The method expands each instruction into an application-specific encoding, removes unused datapath and decode logic during synthesis, and yields cores that remain assembler-compatible with the original program while no longer being binary-compatible with a general-purpose RISC-V. We implement example designs on RV32I (base integer), RV32M (integer multiply), and RV32F (single-precision floating-point) configurations. Our optimized RISC-V is as small as 170 ALMs and closes timing at 775 MHz in an Altera Agilex-5 device. Finally, we show that these processors can be packed into a deterministic area and stepped-and-repeated continuously without material impact on performance, enabling predictable multi-core density planning.
item.author: cs.AR updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs.AR updates on arXiv.org] Compiling Multi-Threshold Operators for Quantized Non-Monotonic and Fine-Granular Activations in Custom-Tailored DNN Accelerators
item.description: arXiv:2610.21825v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Aggressive quantization of neural networks can expose activation functions as bottlenecks for efficient hardware acceleration. Implementing quantized activations as multi-threshold operations has been shown to be a promising optimization, allowing for efficient hardware implementation of few-bit activations. However, current implementations are limited to monotonically increasing functions, quantization schemes with one-dimensional (per-channel) granularity and a small set of predefined activation-quantizer combinations. We formalize the multi-threshold representation to extend it to non-monotonic functions and fine-granular parameters, i.e., multi-dimensional thresholds. For automated conversion of quantized function compositions into threshold representation, we propose a systematic approach via algebraic rules integrated into the ONNX-based compiler infrastructure. We experimentally validate our solution on a selection of monotonic and non-monotonic functions by extending the binary search based multi-threshold operator that is integrated into the FINN framework for end-to-end synthesis of custom-tailored FPGA accelerators. The cost of hardware support for non-monotonicity and fine-granularity is characterized in comparison to an alternative approach utilizing existing operators via graph-level decomposition. We compare our method to prior work as well as the approach taken by the hls4ml framework. As an outlook, we demonstrate the prospects of using the multi-threshold representation during the training of a neural network as a form of quantization aware training.
item.author: cs.AR updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs.AR updates on arXiv.org] Arcal\'{i}s: Accelerating Remote Procedure Calls Using a L\'{i}ghtweight Near-Cache Solution
item.description: arXiv:2602.12596v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Modern microservices increasingly depend on high-performance remote procedure calls (RPCs) to coordinate fine-grained, distributed computation. As network bandwidths continue to scale, the CPU overhead associated with RPC processing, particularly serialization, deserialization, and protocol handling, has become a critical bottleneck. This challenge is exacerbated by fast user-space networking stacks such as DPDK, which expose RPC processing as the dominant performance limiter. While prior hardware accelerators have explored NIC-attached and FPGA-based offload, these approaches remain farther from the cache hierarchy, so the frequent data accesses during RPC processing each pay an extra interconnect traversal cost that inflates RPC time. Therefore, RPC handling should occur as close as possible to the cache; however, a near-cache solution must be small, hence practical and deployable. Our key insight to enable such a solution is taking advantage of a reconfigurable accelerator that can be configured specifically for the services currently running on the CPUs. We present Arcal\'{\i}s, a near-cache RPC accelerator that positions a lightweight hardware engine adjacent to the last-level cache (LLC). Arcal\'{\i}s offloads RPC processing to dedicated microengines that operate with cache-line latency while preserving programmability. By decoupling RPC processing logic, enabling microservice-specific execution, and positioning itself near the LLC, Arcal\'{\i}s achieves a 1.72-4.91$\times$ end-to-end speedup compared to the CPU baseline, significantly reduces microarchitectural overhead by up to 88\%, and achieves up to a 1.67$\times$ higher throughput than prior solutions. These results highlight the potential of near-cache RPC acceleration as a practical solution for high-performance microservice deployment.
item.author: cs.AR updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs.AR updates on arXiv.org] FAME: An FPGA-Based Platform for Approximate Multipliers Evaluation with Pattern-Guided DNN Retraining
item.description: arXiv:2609.17730v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Approximate multipliers can reduce hardware area and energy consumption in Deep Neural Network (DNN) inference; however, they introduce computational errors. Assessing the accuracy of numerous approximate multiplier designs across diverse DNN models and large-scale datasets remains challenging due to prohibitive evaluation times. This overhead primarily stems from the slow emulation of approximate multiplier behavior using look-up tables (LUTs) on CPU and GPU platforms. Moreover, the resulting accuracy degradation must be carefully quantified and, if necessary, mitigated (e.g., through retraining), further increasing the overall evaluation cost. To address these challenges, we propose FAME, an FPGA-based platform for evaluating approximate multipliers. The platform exploits the reconfigurable logic of Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) to implement approximate multipliers directly in hardware, eliminating the need for LUT-based emulation on CPU/GPU platforms and thereby enabling efficient DNN inference while significantly reducing evaluation time on large datasets. Furthermore, we introduce a pattern-guided DNN retraining technique to mitigate accuracy degradation induced by approximate multipliers. Specifically, retraining is guided by multiplier-specific patterns to effectively recover potential accuracy losses. We evaluate FAME using two DNN models, ResNet-18 and MobileNetV2, on the ImageNet dataset across 27 approximate multipliers. During inference, our approach achieves up to a 3.47x speedup in approximate multiplier evaluation compared to prior LUT-based emulation methods. Furthermore, the proposed retraining technique improves accuracy by up to 65.5% over existing retraining approaches for the evaluated multipliers. The code is publicly available at: https://github.com/gicLAB/FAME
