item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Frustrated Topological Orbital Magnetism
item.description: arXiv:2610.12557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By studying the interplay of geometric frustration with Aharonov-Bohm fluxes in three dimensions, we unveil a rich playground exhibiting topological semimetallic ground states with orbital magnetic dipole, quadrupole and ferrotoroidic orders, akin to spin patterns in classical spin ices - a class of phenomena which we dub frustrated topological orbital magnetism. We demonstrate that the ground-state toroidizations underpinned by non-Abelian topological nodal lines induce measurable current-induced Hall phenomena. We further find that distinct 2-in-2-out and 3-in-1-out frustrated orbital current patterns can be associated with topological Weyl node charges, and corresponding anisotropic linear and nonlinear Hall effects. We propose signatures for experimental validation of distinct frustrated topological orbital magnetic orders in candidate materials.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Homogeneous to multi-scale inhomogeneous complex magnetism in Ba3LnRu2O9 (Ln = Gd, Ho), Revealed by muSR and Machine-Learned Muon-Site Calculations
item.description: arXiv:2610.12726v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report a comprehensive muon spin rotation and relaxation (muSR) study of the hexagonal 6H-perovskites Ba3LnRu2O9 (Ln = Gd, Ho) to investigate the role of rare-earth anisotropy in the magnetic ground state of 4d-4f coupled systems. Ba3HoRu2O9 exhibits two successive magnetic orderings at TN1 = 46 K and TN2 = 10 K, leading to a complex magnetic ground state, whereas Ba3GdRu2O9, with Gd3+ (L = 0) S-state ions, shows primarily single magnetic ordering at TN = 14.5 K. Zero-field (ZF) and longitudinal-field (LF) muSR measurements reveal markedly different magnetic behavior despite their structural similarity. Ba3HoRu2O9 displays a multi-scale inhomogeneous magnetic state characterized by two-component exponential relaxation, broad local-field distributions, incomplete LF decoupling, and persistent spin dynamics. The muSR results identify two characteristic magnetic energy scales near 46 and 10 K, associated with correlated Ru-Ho interactions and quasistatic magnetic ordering, respectively. Redfield analysis further demonstrates strong local magnetic fields and distributed spin fluctuation timescales, confirming magnetic inhomogeneity. Machine-learning-assisted muon-site and dipolar-field calculations show that the broad field distribution naturally arises from muons sensing distinct coexisting magnetic domains at different structural sites. In contrast, Ba3GdRu2O9 exhibits a comparatively homogeneous antiferromagnetic ground state below 14.5 K, with Gaussian relaxation consistent with a narrow static field distribution. These results establish that the rare-earth ion in Ba3LnRu2O9 is a powerful tuning parameter, driving the ground state from homogeneous to complex, multi-scale inhomogeneous behavior through competing 4d-4f magnetic interactions.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Room-temperature ferroelectric p-wave magnet
item.description: arXiv:2610.12892v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: P -wave magnets exhibit odd-parity spin polarization in momentum space while retaining zero net magnetization, offering a promising route toward nonrelativistic spintronics. Previously reported p-wave magnets based on combined time-reversal and lattice-translation symmetry, Tt, have thus far exhibited ordering temperatures below the liquid-nitrogen range. Here, we demonstrate a distinct route to a pristine p-wave magnetism that does not require T t symmetry, and instead is based on incommensurate spin-spiral order. Specifically, the cycloidal magnetic structure of the multiferroic BiFeO3 (BFO) intrinsically realizes p-wave magnetism coexisting with ferroelectric polarization at room temperature. Combining symmetry analysis, density-functional-theory calculations, and circular photogalvanic-effect (CPGE) measurements, we find a large nonrelativistic spin splitting of approximately 100 meV associated with the cycloidal order. The resulting p-wave spin polarization gives rise to a characteristic CPGE response whose sign can be reversibly switched by electrically controlling the cycloid chirality. Our results establish ferroelectric BiFeO3 as a room-temperature platform for electrically switchable p-wave magnetism and provide a route toward voltage-controlled spintronic devices based on parity-breaking magnetic order.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Symmetry-Enforced Topology and Van Hove Saddle Points in Hexagonal TiAs
item.description: arXiv:2610.12925v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report the first successful growth of stoichiometric hexagonal TiAs single crystals (space group $P6_3/mmc$) using chemical vapor transport and investigate their vibrational, electronic, topological, and magnetotransport properties. Polarized Raman spectroscopy identifies all four Raman-active phonon modes ($A_{1g} + E_{1g} + 2E_{2g}$), consistent with the hexagonal crystal symmetry. First-principles calculations reveal nontrivial band topology characterized by a symmetry indicator $\mathbb{Z}_4 = 2$ and a strong topological index $\nu_0 = 1$, together with symmetry-protected fourfold band degeneracies at the nonsymmorphic Brillouin-zone boundary. The Fermi surface exhibits an orbital-dependent crossover from quasi-two-dimensional cylindrical sheets to a corrugated three-dimensional structure along $k_z$. A Van Hove saddle point approximately 0.5 eV below the Fermi level along $\Gamma\text{--}K$ is associated with a neck-disrupting Lifshitz transition and enhanced density of states. Magnetotransport measurements reveal a pronounced twofold angular magnetoresistance, consistent with anisotropic Fermi-surface geometry and open cyclotron orbits. Hall measurements indicate uncompensated, hole-dominated transport, accounting for the absence of extreme magnetoresistance and contributing to the field-orientation-dependent Hall response. These results establish hexagonal TiAs as a platform for exploring the interplay of nonsymmorphic band topology, Van Hove singularities, and anisotropic electronic transport in transition-metal monopnictides.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Vacuum-field-mediated Landau-level reconstruction in a cavity-coupled two-dimensional electron gas
item.description:
arXiv:2610.12956v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a two-dimensional electron gas in the integer quantum Hall regime coupled to a single spatially modulated cavity mode in the static off-resonant limit. Retaining both paramagnetic and diamagnetic contributions on equal footing, we derive a gauge complete single-particle Hamiltonian in which virtual photon exchange generates a periodic kinetic renormalization and a diamagnetic scalar potential. Both terms transfer momentum by $2k_0$ and displace guiding centers by $\Delta X=2k_0\ell_B^2$, forming a finite-$k_0$ momentum ladder. Diagonalizing the strip Hamiltonian, we find that the ladder reconstructs the Landau-level band structure and redistributes, rather than multiplies, the associated chiral edge states. Occupied-subspace Chern numbers remain $C_
u=
u$ for $
u=1,2,3$ throughout $0\le\lambda_{\mathrm{cav}}\le 0.5$, while the bulk gaps decrease without closing. Strip Kubo responses show cavity-induced displacements of the Hall-step energies; at finite width the plateau heights are noninteger and approach the integers as $L_x$ increases. The ladder is spectrally resolved at $k_0\ell_B=0.5$ and collapses at $k_0\ell_B=0.1$. These results isolate a spatially local, finite-$k_0$ momentum ladder as a clean-system mechanism by which a structured vacuum field reconstructs quantum Hall spectra and strip transport without changing the integer topology, complementary to cavity-mediated all-to-all hopping.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Scalene Yang-Baxter triples realize all nearest-neighbour Hamiltonians with global additive symmetries
item.description: arXiv:2610.13782v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish that bond Hamiltonian densities, up to local difference terms whose sum vanishes under periodic boundary conditions, lying in the commutant of bond operators, $w_j\pm w_{j+1}$, is a necessary and sufficient condition for a one-dimensional nearest-neighbour Hamiltonian to conserve a uniform or staggered sum of the one-site operators $w_j$. Starting from these local commutants, we show that every such Hamiltonian and its conserved charge can be obtained from monodromy matrices constructed using regular and non-regular members of scalene Yang-Baxter triples. The results hold on periodic chains of length $L\geq3$, with even length required in the staggered case. The results do not require translation invariance, and hence the interaction on each bond can be chosen independently from the full corresponding commutant. Our representation-independent construction applies in arbitrary finite local dimension and exhausts the Hamiltonians with either prescribed additive symmetry, without requiring ordinary Yang-Baxter integrability. We illustrate the construction with spin-$\tfrac12$ and spin-1 systems and discuss its relation to the double-commutant theorem. Classifying the one-site generators $w$ and their associated bond commutants provides a route to classifying such Hamiltonians with additive conserved charges.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Improved screening of doped ZrO$_2$ catalysts for CO$_2$ hydrogenation from graph-based machine learning
item.description: arXiv:2610.13795v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dopants can tune the activity of zirconia-based CO$_2$ hydrogenation catalysts through changes in adsorbate and transition-state (TS) energetics. Computing these quantities with density functional theory (DFT) becomes expensive when several dopants, reaction intermediates, and TSs must be screened. Here, we further develop the graph-based machine learning method Wasserstein Weisfeiler-Lehman Gaussian Process Regression (WWL-GPR): we introduce additional electronic-structure and local-environment features relevant for oxide surfaces and use the resulting model to predict adsorption and TS energies on ZrO$_2$(101) surfaces doped with Al$^{3+}$, Cd$^{2+}$, Ga$^{3+}$, In$^{3+}$, and Zn$^{2+}$. Adsorbate-surface structures are represented as attributed graphs that combine bonds connectivity and features. We benchmark WWL-GPR against thermodynamic scaling relations (TSR) for reaction intermediates and Bronsted-Evans-Polanyi relations (BEP) for TSs, and then propagate the predicted energies to microkinetic CH$_3$OH-yield estimates. WWL-GPR consistently improves the prediction of reaction intermediate energetics relative to linear scaling approaches and provides TS estimates that are competitive with BEP-based models. These improvements become especially relevant when the predicted energetics are propagated through the reaction network. Microkinetic calculations show that WWL-GPR-derived energies give CH$_3$OH yields closer to DFT-derived yields than the linear-relation workflow. Degree-of-rate-control analysis links the activity errors to dopant-dependent rate-controlling steps, including HCOO* formation, H$_2$COOH* dissociation, and H$_3$CO* formation. These results support WWL-GPR as a data-efficient surrogate for connecting atomistic energetics with catalyst-screening observables on doped oxide surfaces.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] An all-transistor physical-learning transformer can be trained to perform in-context learning
item.description: arXiv:2610.12571v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Most systems trained by equilibrium propagation or coupled learning are in the same class as multi-layer perceptrons: while they may be universal function approximators, they struggle to learn associative tasks which are easy for transformers. Equilibrium propagation relies on a bidirectional flow of information through the physical system between input and output. The reverse flow is broken by more complex nonlinear systems, such as those performing multiplication which is needed to express dot-product attention. Here we explicitly restore this bidirectional flow by introducing extra circuit elements for this purpose into a double or dyadic circuit. We then use these ideas to construct an attention mechanism exploiting the exponential current law of sub-threshold MOSFET devices. We show that in simulations this circuit can be trained to perform a simple in-context learning task, despite using realistic reverse components which transmit only an approximate gradient. For this training to succeed we need cross-entropy loss (not mean squared error). We generate nudges appropriate for this loss using a novel floating circuit element, based on the same MOSFET sub-circuit used for softmax. We train the resistors in this circuit using the Lion optimiser, which can be implemented using one capacitor per parameter to store local memory of past gradient estimates.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Separating Field--Camp Alignment from Structural Balance in a Frustrated Random-Field Ising Model of Social Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.12578v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Frustrated Ising models of social networks mix ferromagnetic (agreement-seeking) and antiferromagnetic (antagonistic) couplings, and the antagonistic bonds are almost always placed independently at a fixed rate, yielding a +/-J spin glass. Real signed networks (Epinions, Slashdot, Wikipedia) instead show an excess of balanced triads, and perfectly balanced placement is gauge-equivalent to an unfrustrated ferromagnet. We compare three sign-placement conditions on a frustrated random-field Ising model of a polarised population, sharing an identical graph, field assignment, and edge-weight magnitudes: an independent baseline; a balance-structured condition whose camp membership coincides with each voter's field sign; and the same condition with camp labels randomly permuted, so triadic balance is identical by construction while the camp-field correlation is removed. On a confound-controlled Kolmogorov-Smirnov test of the sampled energy-gap distribution (simulated annealing), the aligned condition differs from the baseline at every density tested (p = 7.3e-8), while the permuted condition shows no significant difference (paired mean difference 0.003, 95% CI [-0.041, 0.046]). Field-camp alignment, not triadic balance alone, drives the effect. The qualitative direction follows from a known mapping; the contribution is a quantitative, confound-controlled measurement of the effect's size away from that limit, robust to parallel-tempering sampling, system sizes up to N = 300, and structural noise calibrated to real networks, while triadic balance alone produces no detectable effect at N = 90 and at most a small one at N = 180-300 (paired change in KS distance about 0.04, 95% CI upper bound below 0.09).
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Zak Phase Quantization without Global Symmetry through Destructive Interference
item.description: arXiv:2610.13250v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Zak phase provides a fundamental geometric characterization of one-dimensional band structures and, when quantized by symmetry, serves as a bulk indicator of polarization and boundary phenomena. Conventionally, its exact quantization is tied to a global symmetry of the Bloch Hamiltonian, such as inversion or reflection symmetry. Here, we demonstrate a distinct mechanism by which the Zak phase remains exactly quantized even when the corresponding protecting symmetry is explicitly broken at the level of the full Hamiltonian. The mechanism is based on local support symmetry and destructive interference: symmetry-breaking degrees of freedom are coupled to a topological parent system in such a way that the relevant Bloch states cannot leak into them. The preserved states therefore retain their parent wave functions and inherit their quantized Zak phase exactly, despite the absence of the protecting global symmetry. We establish this mechanism for general one-dimensional insulators and demonstrate it in an inversion-broken minimal model and a reflection-broken armchair nanoribbon, where a quantized $\pi$ Zak phase and associated boundary-localized states persist. We further show that perturbations violating the exact destructive-interference condition continuously dequantize the Zak phase, while a finite regime with a near-$\pi$ Zak phase and boundary response can survive. Our results establish wave-function support, rather than global symmetry alone, as a mechanism for protecting quantized quantum geometry in one-dimensional systems.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Modular Properties of Generalised Gibbs Ensembles: The Deformed KdV Hierarchy
item.description: arXiv:2610.13875v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a set of conserved charges which are deformations of quantum KdV charges. They are associated with the modular transformation of a GGE with the spin-$\sigma$ KdV charge inserted with chemical potential $\alpha_\sigma$. The charges are formal power series in the chemical potential, with coefficients given by local integrals of motion. We define local recursion relations and equivalent flow equations, prove commutativity to all orders, and establish uniqueness of the currents modulo total derivatives for a fixed generating series. We show that the eigenvalues of these deformed charges can be obtained from the thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz in two models. In the $c=1/2$ free fermion theory, the deformed charges reduce to explicit linear combinations of undeformed KdV charges, and their ground-state eigenvalues agree with the TBA expansion to all orders. In the Lee-Yang model, we find numerical agreement through cubic order in the spin-$5$ deformation for the first few charges evaluated on low-lying states.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson Volumes from the Spectral Edge of DSSYK and Supersymmetric Extensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.13899v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson volumes of Do and Norbury are the top-degree parts of Okuyama's discrete volumes, which are defined by topological recursion on the spectral curve of the double-scaled SYK (DSSYK) model. We show that the same q-deformed volumes can be obtained from a double-scaled matrix model whose disk density is found by zooming in on the soft edges of the DSSYK density. Applying the same procedure to the hard edge of $\mathcal{N}=1$ DSSYK, we obtain candidate $q$-deformed $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes. They are polynomials of fixed degree, and they reduce to the $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes in a scaled $q\to1$ limit. These candidate volumes differ from the $\mathcal{N}=1$ volumes of Do and Norbury in (arXiv:2510.12431) up to what we call "irrelevant" contributions which exactly vanish in the scaled $q\to 1$ limit. Together, these results demonstrate how q-deformed volumes can be naturally associated to the spectral edges of various DSSYK models and provides an intuitive way to construct them in supersymmetric contexts.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Specific-heat anomaly in frustrated magnets with vacancy defects
item.description: arXiv:2506.17392v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by frustrated magnets and spin-liquid-candidate materials, we study the thermodynamics of a 2D geometrically frustrated magnet with vacancy defects. The presence of vacancies imposes significant constraints on the bulk spins, which freeze some of the degrees of freedom in the system at low temperatures. With increasing temperature, these constraints get relaxed, resulting in an increase in the system's entropy. This leads to the emergence of a peak in the heat capacity $C(T)$ of the magnet at a temperature $T_\text{imp}$ determined by the concentration of the vacancy defects. The entropy associated with this peak comes from the lowest-energy degrees of freedom in the material. To illustrate the emergence of such an anomaly, we compute analytically the heat capacity of the antiferromagnetic (AFM) Ising model on the triangular lattice with vacancy defects. The presence of the vacancy leads to a peak in $C(T)$ at the temperature $T_\text{imp}=-4J/\ln n_\text{imp}$, where $J$ is the AFM coupling between the spins and $n_\text{imp}$ is the fraction of the missing sites.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Anomalous Edge Contrast in Magnetic Force Imaging of 2D Topological Insulators
item.description: arXiv:2602.18281v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Magnetic force imaging (MFM) of 2D topological insulators, such as crystalline plates of Bi2Te3 and Bi2Se3, reveals anomalously large contrast around the plate edges even under ambient imaging conditions. And while there are several known contrast mechanisms in MFM, these cannot easily explain the magnitude of contrast observe for such systems. In this work we use multi-parameter magnetic force phase imaging together with a simple analytical model to suggest that the observed magnetic edge-features can be associated with two sources: a pseudo-Faraday effect in the conductive edge channels of the topological system and magnetic scattering in those channels caused by the proximal, localized field of the tip. These results suggest novel MFM contrast mechanisms unique to topological systems and point to the utility of multi-parameter MFM techniques in studies of topological-material-based circuit elements.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Pressure and Size Dependence of Roton Emission and Vortex Creation by Moving Objects in He~II in $T \to 0$ Limit: Generalized Nonlocal Gross-Pitaevskii Model
item.description: arXiv:2605.24075v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the framework of generalized, nonlocal Gross-Pitaevskii (GP) model, we study numerically the pressure- and size-dependent mechanisms of roton emission and vortex nucleation by objects moving in superfluid $^4$He. As far as the authors are aware, this is the first attempt to analyze the pressure dependence of these mechanisms and the associated critical velocities within a single theoretical framework. For each of several pressures in the range from 0 to the solidification pressure of $\approx25$~bar, we chose the parameters of the interatomic interaction potential such that the resulting excitation spectrum for the generalized, nonlocal GP equation approximates fairly accurately the pressure-dependent dispersion curve determined experimentally by Godfrin \textit{et al.}, Phys. Rev. B \textbf{103}, 104516 (2021). In the two-dimensional approximation, for circular obstacles (disks) moving in quiescent $^4$He, we calculated two critical velocities -- one corresponding to the roton emission and the other to the nucleation of quantized vortices -- as functions of pressure and the obstacle's size. We also comment briefly on three-dimensional simulations of the roton emission and vortex nucleation by moving spherical obstacles.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Instabilities in self-consistent diagrammatic approaches and how to cure them
item.description: arXiv:2609.11405v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: While self-consistent diagrammatic approaches are widely used to compute the physical properties of correlated quantum materials, their applicability may get severely hindered precisely in the parameter regions where the most exciting physics is observed. One of the major issues, referred to as "misleading convergence", is the tendency of iterative schemes to converge to unphysical fixed points for intermediate-to-strong electronic interactions, regardless of the numerical accuracy of the computation. Here, we explicitly verify that the origin of this problem in several established self-consistent many-electron approaches, defined in the general diagrammatic framework of the boson-exchange formalism, resides exclusively in the stability condition of the respective iteration schemes, and not in an intrinsic breakdown of their self-consistent diagrammatic description. This insight enables a simple and general remedy, as recently proposed in Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016502 (2026): The redefinition of the iterative procedure, by inverting the unstable eigendirections of the Jacobian associated with the fixed point of the self-consistent algorithm. We illustrate the successful outcome of this procedure by means of systematic calculations performed on exactly solvable testbed models. Our results demonstrate that the physical fixed point of the diagrammatic schemes we considered can be stabilized, de facto, across the entire parameter range, including the most challenging nonperturbative/strong-coupling regimes.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Proof of a Universal Speed Limit on Fast Scrambling in Quantum Systems
item.description: arXiv:2404.15403v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the time required for sustained information scrambling in any Hamiltonian quantum system is universally at least logarithmic in the entanglement entropy of scrambled states. This addresses two foundational problems in nonequilibrium quantum dynamics. (1) It sets the earliest possible time for the applicability of equilibrium statistical mechanics in a quantum system coupled to a bath at a finite temperature. (2) It proves a version of the fast scrambling conjecture, originally motivated in models associated with black holes, as a fundamental property of quantum mechanics itself. Our result builds on a refinement of the energy-time uncertainty principle in terms of the infinite temperature spectral form factor in quantum chaos. We generalize this formulation to arbitrary initial states of the bath, including finite temperature states, by mapping Hamiltonian dynamics with any initial state to nonunitary dynamics at infinite temperature. A regularized spectral form factor emerges naturally from this procedure, whose decay is universally constrained by analyticity in complex time. This establishes an exact speed limit on information scrambling by the most general quantum mechanical Hamiltonian, without any restrictions on locality or the nature of interactions.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Bulk OPE Coefficients of the $E$-Series Virasoro Minimal Models
item.description: arXiv:2609.25215v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present bulk-primary operator-product coefficients for every Virasoro minimal model with an $E_6$, $E_7$, or $E_8$ modular invariant. Dividing by a universal product of chiral generalized-minimal-model OPE coefficients reduces the conformal bootstrap problem to a finite algebraic problem governed by root-of-unity quantum-group $6j$ symbols. The exceptional factors of the OPE coefficients can be chosen independent of the second Kac indices $s$, and their dependence on the central charge reduces to finitely many reference cases and explicit phases. A finite computer-assisted calculation yields candidate algebraic $s=1$ seed data and high-precision numerical evidence for existence and uniqueness modulo primary-field signs. We prove that exact existence and uniqueness for these seeds imply the corresponding result for all Kac labels within the genus-zero bulk locality and crossing equations; the finite seed step remains uncertified. The three families require $18$, $32$, and $107$ representative reduced OPE coefficients for $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$, respectively. We provide reconstruction conventions and coefficient tables for both unitary and nonunitary models. Our calculation assumes only Virasoro symmetry, bulk locality (permutation symmetry) and OPE associativity (crossing equations).
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs.AR updates on arXiv.org] Anechoic: Onsager-Corrected Parallel Annealing for Sub-0.1 ms Dense Max-Cut on an FPGA
item.description: arXiv:2610.13368v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ising machines solve combinatorial optimization problems by annealing a network of spins. On dense problems, the least expensive hardware step updates all spins at once: stochastic cellular automata (SCA) decide every spin in parallel and read couplings only for the spins that flip. Such synchronous updates create an echo: the previous state of each spin returns to it through its neighbors. On K2000, a Max-Cut benchmark on a 2,000-node complete graph, two-thirds of all flips undo the same spin's flip one step earlier. This paper presents Anechoic, an FPGA Ising machine that subtracts this echo from every decision. Dynamical mean-field theory identifies the echo as an Onsager reaction; its one-step strength is the number of spins whose flip probability is strictly between 0 and 1, divided by twice the temperature. The decision logic already flags these spins, so the correction costs one population count per step; a temperature-scaled form needs none. An RTL engine executes a dense 2,000-spin step in 18.1 cycles plus 0.14 per flip, so every saved step and flip saves time. Both forms find better K2000 cuts at every step budget than five published binary-spin algorithms at their papers' settings. Twelve engines at 250 MHz on an AMD Alveo V80 reach a cut of at least 33,000 with 99% probability in 0.05 ms, 5.2 times faster than the fastest published hardware, at 5.4 mJ per solution; with 2-bit couplings, the temperature-scaled form is also faster than uncorrected SCA on 49 of 51 G-set graphs. On an NVIDIA GH200 GPU, the same engine is 2.3 times slower and needs 8.0 times more energy per solution, though its 240 concurrent anneals give 2.3 times the throughput. As a GlobalFoundries 22 nm ASIC at 1.25 GHz, twelve engines would reach the target in about 10 microseconds, 26 times faster than the fastest published hardware. The code is available at https://github.com/skethz/anechoic.
item.author: cs.AR updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs.AR updates on arXiv.org] Power, Performance, and Area of HPC-Based Malware Detectors: An FPGA and Open-PDK ASIC Study
item.description: arXiv:2610.12795v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hardware malware detectors (HMDs) classify programs as benign or malicious based on hardware performance counter (HPC) data. Previous studies have shown that ensemble classifiers outperform other classifiers on detection metrics. However, the area, power, and timing costs of HMDs remain open questions. We address these questions across a comprehensive design space comprising multiple classifier families, variable HPC sets, and ensemble learning methods. We designed a pipeline to reconstruct selected trained models, generate synthesizable register-transfer-level (RTL) implementations, validate each design against a bit-accurate golden model, and evaluate the implementations. The results show that tree- and rule-based detectors achieve the highest detection performance with nearly an order of magnitude less area and several times lower energy than function-based classifiers. Reducing the number of HPC inputs to fit a processor's concurrent-counter limit preserves detection performance while substantially reducing area, power, and delay.

item.title: [Applied Physics Letters Current Issue] Phonon transport in layered NaMnO 2 : Roles of interlayer electrostatic coupling and Jahn–Teller distortions
item.description: Sodium-ion batteries offer a sustainable alternative to lithium-based systems, but their safety and performance can be affected by inadequate thermal management during high-rate operation. Here, we present a first-principles investigation of lattice thermal transport in representative layered NaxMnO2 structural models, including the fully desodiated δ-MnO2 limit ( x=0), an intermediate-composition O3′-Na0.5MnO2 model ( x=0.5), and fully sodiated O3′-NaMnO2 and P2′-NaMnO2 polymorphs ( x=1). Using the Boltzmann transport equation combined with the Wigner transport formalism, we reveal pronounced variations in both the magnitude and anisotropy of lattice thermal conductivity among these structural models. Relative to desodiated δ-MnO2, Na+ insertion redistributes charge and strengthens electrostatic interactions between the inserted Na+ layer and adjacent oxygen layers, thereby enhancing out-of-plane phonon transport. Meanwhile, the Mn3+-associated Jahn–Teller distortion softens selected in-plane Mn–O linkages and suppresses the corresponding in-plane thermal transport. These structural changes modify phonon dispersions, group velocities, and mean free paths, resulting in a substantial reduction in thermal conductivity anisotropy in the sodiated models. Our results clarify how Na content, interlayer interactions, and Jahn–Teller distortions jointly regulate anisotropic phonon transport in layered manganese oxides, providing insight relevant to thermal management in sodium-ion battery cathodes.
item.author: Applied Physics Letters Current Issue

item.title: [Applied Physics Letters Current Issue] p -type Ohmic contact engineering in TMDs via MoO 3 -induced interface dipoles
item.description: Two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenide (TMD) electronics are often limited by high contact resistance arising from Fermi-level pinning and van der Waals tunneling barriers. Conventional bulk-doping approaches are generally incompatible with atomically thin materials because they can cause severe lattice damage, whereas interfacial charge-transfer doping offers a nondestructive alternative. Here, we investigate a monolayer MoO3 interlayer inserted between metal electrodes and TMD channels to realize p-type Ohmic contacts. First-principles calculations show that the high electron affinity of MoO3 drives electron transfer from the TMD and generates interfacial dipoles that shift the TMD Fermi level toward the valence-band edge. The MoO3 interlayer also spatially separates the metal from the TMD, thereby reducing gap states associated with direct metal–TMD hybridization. The contact properties of metal–MoO3–TMD heterostructures depend strongly on the MoO3–TMD band alignment: type-II MoO3–MoS2 interfaces exhibit reduced but generally finite hole Schottky barriers, whereas type-III MoO3–WSe2 interfaces produce favorable p-type Ohmic contacts. Density-functional-theory-based nonequilibrium Green's function simulations further predict enhanced on-state currents in MoO3-intercalated devices under idealized ballistic conditions. These results identify band-alignment-controlled interfacial dipoles as the dominant mechanism by which atomically thin MoO3 improves p-type TMD contacts for two-dimensional complementary electronics.
item.author: Applied Physics Letters Current Issue

item.title: [Applied Physics Letters Current Issue] Device-aware compensation of nonideal spintronic synapses for electrocardiogram classification using spiking neural networks
item.description: Spintronic synapses offer a promising route toward low-power neuromorphic hardware for edge intelligence. Their nonvolatility, multilevel tunability, and compatibility with event-driven spiking neural networks (SNNs) make them attractive for temporal biomedical signal processing. Moving beyond conventional demonstrations of synaptic plasticity, here we examine how nonideal spin–orbit torque (SOT) synaptic updates affect SNN learning and how they can be compensated. TaMo/CoFeB/MgO/Ta SOT devices with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy exhibit nonvolatile multilevel anomalous Hall resistance states and reversible long-term potentiation and depression. Combined finite-element and micromagnetic simulations indicate that the nonlinear weight evolution is closely associated with spatially nonuniform SOT-driven domain dynamics. Incorporating the measured update curves into an SNN for MIT-BIH electrocardiogram abnormal-beat classification shows that device nonideality strongly degrades recognition of minority-class abnormal beats. A device-aware compensation strategy restores balanced effective updates, bringing the overall accuracy close to the ideal-update reference (95.06% vs 95.23%). It also increases the F1 score for the minority F-class abnormal beats from 11.86% to 64.08%. This work highlights device-aware compensation as an effective route for translating nonideal spintronic synapses into practical low-power biomedical neuromorphic hardware. Such hardware is promising for wearable health-monitoring applications.
item.author: Applied Physics Letters Current Issue

item.title: [Applied Physics Letters Current Issue] Indentation size effect in Mg 2 C 60 governed by depth-dependent activation of shear bands and localized amorphization
item.description: Indentation size effects in crystalline solids are commonly associated with dislocation-mediated strain gradients. Here, we show that the layered molecular crystal Mg2C60 exhibits a distinct small-scale response. Continuous stiffness nanoindentation reveals that both hardness and modulus increase as the indentation depth decreases from 1 μm to 100 nm, notably deviating from classical dislocation-based predictions. Cross-sectional focused ion beam–transmission electron microscopy further reveals an evolution from relatively sparse, preferentially oriented shear bands at 0.5 μm to a spatially extended, multi-oriented shear-band network at 1 μm, with localized amorphization confined to selected shear-localized regions. The mechanical measurements and structural observations support a depth-dependent evolution from a more confined deformation state toward distributed shear localization at larger indentation depths. The results demonstrate that bonding hierarchy and structural discreteness, rather than conventional strain-gradient hardening alone, govern the depth-dependent indentation response of Mg2C60.
item.author: Applied Physics Letters Current Issue

item.title: [Applied Physics Letters Current Issue] Competing hysteresis mechanisms in HZO/MoS 2 transistors with a metal–ferroelectric–metal–insulator–semiconductor gate stack
item.description: Ferroelectric field-effect transistors based on hafnium oxide offer a versatile platform for advanced memory concepts. Here, we demonstrate a proof-of-concept top-gated Hf0.5Zr0.5O2-based transistor integrating a metal–ferroelectric–metal–insulator–semiconductor (MFMIS) gate stack with a two-dimensional MoS2 channel. The implementation of such an architecture is particularly challenging in MoS2, where the strong sensitivity of the channel to trapped charge can further complicate the balance between ferroelectric switching and charge redistribution within the MFMIS stack. By varying the MFM-to-MIS area ratio and the applied gate-voltage amplitude, we observe a systematic evolution of the transfer hysteresis consistent with competing ferroelectric polarization switching and trap-related contributions. Temperature-dependent measurements, zero-bias write/read experiments, and compact Simulation Program with Integrated Circuit Emphasis modeling provide additional support for this interpretation. Despite the non-optimized gate stack, a substantial ferroelectric contribution to the device response is retained, while retention measurements reveal limitations associated with depolarization and trapping. These results demonstrate the feasibility of MFMIS ferroelectric transistors based on MoS2 and provide a basis for further optimization of their gate-stack design and memory performance.

item.title: [Nature Communications] Intensification of near-inertial currents in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78555-0

Ocean drifter observations reveal that Atlantic near-inertial currents intensified by almost 4% per decade during 2003–2022. This intensification is primarily driven by changes in wind forcing associated with mesoscale weather systems.

item.title: [Nature Communications] A supergene and genomic mosaicism are associated with phenotypic evolution in Galápagos tree finches
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78507-8

Adaptive radiations produce striking phenotypic diversity over remarkably short evolutionary timescales. This study uses genomic analyses of Darwin’s tree finches to reveal a cryptic lineage, in which autosomal differentiation with another sympatric species is restricted primarily to a single locus (G03) that approaches fixation, shifting them from one phenotypic optimum to another.

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Axiomatic Incompatibility Between Thermal Equilibrium and Volume-Dependent Entropy in Ideal Gas Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.10645v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A rigorous macroscopic analysis of classical thermodynamics reveals an overlooked contradiction at the foundations of ideal gas theory: the traditional volume dependent formula for entropy violates the fundamental axiom of thermal equilibrium during reversible isothermal processes. This paper resolves this inconsistency by establishing a strict operational distinction between strictly isothermal and quasi isothermal processes. We show that in order for the perfect gas to be strictly consistent with the laws of classical thermodynamics, the thermodynamic entropy of a perfect gas must be a function of temperature only. This independence of volume is also confirmed by a new analysis of the adiabatic free expansion of an ideal gas, which is found to be intrinsically reversible. To reconcile these results with standard thermodynamic practice, we introduce the concept of a pseudo isothermal process (a finite sequence of small adiabatic and isochoric steps) and show that the classical equations for work and heat apply rigorously to these real processes, as opposed to strictly isothermal ones. We conclude by discussing the profound implications of these findings for statistical mechanics, showing that while the corrected thermodynamic entropy is in perfect agreement with Maxwell's kinetic theory, it is essentially different from the Planck Boltzmann formula. Thus, thermodynamic entropy and statistical microstate counting are two different physical quantities, and the present analysis provides a simple way to free classical thermodynamics from the paradoxes of microscopic disorder.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Efficiency fluctuations in quantum heat engines with non-quasi-static adiabatic strokes
item.description: arXiv:2610.10647v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We have presented an analytical and numerical study of efficiency fluctuations in quantum Carnot and Otto engines with pistons operating under non-quasi-static adiabatic expansion and compression processes at constant speed, along with quasi-static isothermal (for the Carnot engine) or isochoric processes (for the Otto engine). We have considered the two-point measurement scheme during the adiabatic strokes in this regard. By considering each of the pistons as a single quantum particle in a 1-D box with a non-quasi-statically movable boundary, we capture the stochastic nature of the work output resulting from the unitary evolution of the quantum mechanical state of the system during non-equilibrium processes. Furthermore, we have explicitly shown how the piston speed during quantum non-equilibrium strokes introduces additional quantum fluctuations that modify the average efficiency of both the engines.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Theory of Topologically Ordered Superfluids in 2+1 Dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.10668v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topologically ordered superfluids (TOSFs) support deconfined, gapped anyonic excitations while remaining gapless because of Goldstone modes. We develop a general framework for characterizing their topological data in $(2+1)$-dimensional bosonic systems with spontaneously broken charge ${\rm U}(1)_{\rm c}$ symmetry. Gauging ${\rm U}(1)_{\rm c}$ maps a TOSF to a gapped topological order enriched by a dual ${\rm U}(1)_{\rm dual}$ symmetry with vanishing Hall conductance, while gauging ${\rm U}(1)_{\rm dual}$ recovers the TOSF. This two-way mapping allows the topological data of the TOSF, including the condensate charge, deconfined anyon content, and topological properties of vortices, to be systematically encoded using the algebraic framework of symmetry-enriched topological orders. In particular, superfluid vortices share the topological properties of flux defects associated with the residual discrete symmetry in the gapped anyon sector. We develop complementary algebraic and field-theoretic formulations of this framework, with the latter also suggesting a natural transition to a gapped topologically ordered phase. Additionally, using parton constructions, we present examples of TOSFs with non-Abelian vortices in bosonic systems.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] EPR as a probe for the mechanisms of chirality-induced spin selectivity in photoinduced charge transfer
item.description: arXiv:2610.10839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Several models for chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) in charge transfer have been proposed, but rarely compared directly with experiments. This step is essential for their validation and future progress of the field. Here we investigate a broad class of radical pair states associated with different microscopic models by computing the related electron-paramagnetic resonance spectra. This allows us to evidence peculiar signatures of different radical pair states, to study their experimental accessibility and identify conditions to verify proposed microscopic models.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Reading Altermagnetic Domains with Photon Drag
item.description: arXiv:2610.10970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Finite photon momentum allows second-order photocurrents in centrosymmetric space groups, where the conventional bulk photovoltaic effect is forbidden. Here we study the photon-drag response of altermagnets and show that its angular dependence reveals both the symmetry of the magnetic order and the N\'eel domain of the sample. For example, when a crystal rotation exchanges the two domains, the domain-even and domain-odd parts of the current appear in different angular harmonics, $4n$ and $4n+2$ for tetragonal $d$-wave altermagnets, so that two measurements rotated by $90^\circ$ on a single domain isolate the domain-odd current. We also find that these microscopic contributions exhibit opposite domain parities depending on light polarization. Under linear light, only the shift term is domain odd, while under circular light, the domain-odd channel switches to the injection, Fermi-surface, and contact principal-value terms. Mirror symmetries fix the angular phase of each harmonic and distinguish $d_{x^2-y^2}$, $d_{xy}$, and $g$-wave order. In contrast, conventional collinear antiferromagnets show no domain-odd photon-drag current, and in tetragonal ferromagnets the two parts share the same harmonics. Although the altermagnetic spin splitting does not require spin-orbit coupling (SOC), SOC is essential to observe the domain-odd charge current. Our work uncovers distinct signatures of altermagnetism in photon drag and provides a route to all optical magnetic readouts of altermagnets.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Bond-Switching Reconstruction in Bare Ti3C2 MXene
item.description: arXiv:2610.11062v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: MXene properties are typically tuned through composition, surface termination, and intercalation, while the metal-carbon framework topology is considered fixed. Here, we demonstrate that this framework can reconstruct. Unconstrained relaxations of biaxially strained bare Ti3C2 yield a dynamically stable polymorph, N, featuring a 15-atom primitive cell, six distinct Ti-C bond classes, and 2.55 {\AA} Ti-Ti pairs. The coherent transformation pathway crosses an 8.47 eV barrier per cell but first reaches another reconstructed minimum, N', lying 1.08 eV below N, revealing a family of bond-switched networks. Phase N lies 7.58 eV per cell above the parent. Reverse barriers along the calculated pathway are 1.50 and 1.98 eV per cell for N and N', respectively. Reconstruction quenches the parent spin polarization, yielding a nonmagnetic metal with a nearly fourfold increase in Fermi-level density of states. Bader and electron-localization analyses suggest charge redistribution from C toward Ti associated with Ti-Ti pairing. In multilayers, reconstructed layers form interlayer Ti-C bonds. A 10% biaxial tension halves the phase-energy difference, and pressure reverses phase ordering near 85 GPa. These results establish bond-switching reconstruction as a mechanically controllable structural degree of freedom in MXenes.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Data-Driven Variable-Exponent Analysis for Photoemission Yield Spectroscopy: An Autonomous Self-Diagnosing Framework Based on Integrated Residual Metrics
item.description: arXiv:2610.11331v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photoemission yield spectroscopy (PYS) is widely used for evaluating the electronic states of materials. As automated materials discovery advances, unsupervised extraction of physical information from ambient-air PYS data becomes important. Conventional fixed-exponent analyses and logarithmic transformations suffer from heteroscedasticity, which destabilizes estimation in low-signal regions. To address this, we propose a data-driven analysis framework based on the 1/n-Scan method, which operates directly in the original signal space, removing the geometric bias inherent in log-transform approaches. We further integrate a self-diagnostic quality-evaluation system that quantifies estimation uncertainty with Akaike weights, together with independent residual metrics--the normalized mean absolute error (NMAE), the RMSE-to-MAE ratio (RMR), the Durbin-Watson (DW) statistic, and a macroscopic metric ($\Delta R^2$)--that distinguish hardware-related data degradation from a physical-model mismatch. Applying the framework to differently doped Si and a polycrystalline Au reference in air, we demonstrate autonomous detection, without assumptions on the emission mechanism, of the breakdown of the single-component approximation in heavily doped p-type Si, arising from the overlap of two emission components with different thresholds, as a statistical anomaly--a decrease in DW below its critical value with an auxiliary increase in $\Delta R^2$, despite sound NMAE and RMR--independently confirmed by a two-component fit ($\Delta$AIC $\approx$ 57, DW recovering from 0.8 to 2.0). For heavily doped n-type Si, the gradual surface evolution was classified as a change within the single-component description. This framework provides a robust, self-diagnosing analysis engine for closed-loop autonomous materials exploration.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Probing $L_z$ Orbital Angular Momentum via Wavefunction-Interference-Induced Charge Order
item.description: arXiv:2610.11633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Orbital angular momentum (OAM) characterization is central to understanding quantum materials such as valley Hall and Rashba systems and, through its connection to Berry curvature, provides key insight into band topology. Conventional OAM detection via photoemission dichroism, however, is susceptible to interference artifacts and is largely restricted to occupied states. Here, we demonstrate a real-space approach to map the $L_z$ OAM character using scanning tunneling microscopy in triangular atomic monolayers. Unlike photoemission, this method exploits interference effects arising from the $L_z$ orbital phase and the Bloch phase associated with neighboring atoms. This shifts the local density of states (LDOS) maxima to distinct Wyckoff positions between atoms, encoding $L_z$ information into characteristic real-space LDOS patterns. We exemplify this approach in 2D quantum materials with contrasting $L_z$ sequences, namely Tl/Si(111) and In/SiC(0001) monolayers, identifying $L_z$-dependent LDOS accumulation associated with distinct topological phases in both systems. Our results establish $L_z$-dependent charge localization as a proxy to atomic obstruction for energetically isolated states in triangular lattices, including transition-metal dichalcogenides.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Predicting plasmonic pole representations of complex dielectric spectra using convolutional neural networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.11698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Extracting spectral properties such as energy position, broadening, and spectral weight from dielectric spectra is critical for interpreting collective electronic excitations in many-body physics. Conventional approaches typically rely on nonlinear fitting procedures that can be computationally demanding and highly sensitive to initialization and fitting choices. In this work, we develop a convolutional neural-network framework for the direct inversion of dielectric spectra into their underlying plasmonic pole structures using a multipole-Pad\'e representation. Rather than training on a constrained database of spectra associated with a specific set of materials, the network is trained entirely on synthetic spectra generated from the analytical multipole-Pad\'e expression with randomized parameters. This enables the network to learn the general mapping between the spectra and their features in an unbiased way, without requiring large, material-specific datasets derived from real materials. We demonstrate that the synthetically trained network generalizes to complex first-principles and experimental dielectric spectra, extracting the underlying pole parameters with high accuracy in a single forward pass. This approach provides an efficient and robust alternative to conventional nonlinear fitting, enabling high-throughput, automated analysis of dielectric spectra across diverse materials and applications.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Electric and Heat Transport in One-Dimensional SNS Junctions with Energy-Dependent Transmission
item.description: arXiv:2610.11713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the phase-independent dc components of the electric and heat currents through a one-dimensional superconductor-normal-metal-superconductor (SNS) junction subject to chemical-potential and temperature differences between two superconducting reservoirs. Using a scattering approach based on the Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations, we incorporate multiple Andreev reflections while retaining the energy dependence of transmission through the normal region. We compare energy-independent, quantum-dot-type, and quantum-point-contact transmission profiles. At low bias, both currents exhibit nonlinear features associated with the superconducting gap and multiple Andreev reflections. Their responses to a temperature difference depend remarkably on the transmission profile. At a small finite bias, the electric current depends weakly on the temperature difference for the energy-independent and quantum-dot-type profiles, whereas the quantum-point-contact profile produces a pronounced nonlinear response. The heat current depends nonlinearly on the temperature difference for all three profiles over the parameter range investigated. These results highlight the role of the transmission profile in nonlinear electric and heat transport through SNS junctions and provide a microscopic reference for related transport studies in mesoscopic fermionic superfluid junctions.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Interlayer ferromagnetic order revealed through pressure-enhanced interlayer exchange coupling in Fe$_3$GaTe$_2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.11731v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Van der Waals ferromagnets possess finite interlayer magnetic coupling despite their layered crystal structures, and this coupling plays an important role in determining their magnetic properties. In this study, we performed magnetization measurements on high-quality Fe$_3$GaTe$_2$ single crystals while selectively tuning the interlayer coupling using hydrostatic pressure. We identified two characteristic temperatures, $T_{\rm inf1}$ and $T_{\rm inf2}$, below the Curie temperature with opposite pressure dependences: $T_{\rm inf1}$ is associated with thermally activated domain-wall depinning, whereas $T_{\rm inf2}$ reflects the formation of interlayer ferromagnetic order. Both temperatures exhibit pronounced pressure dependences, in sharp contrast to the nearly pressure-independent Curie temperature associated with intralayer ferromagnetic order. First-principles calculations revealed a substantial pressure-induced enhancement of the interlayer exchange interaction and reasonably reproduced $T_{\rm inf2}$ and its pressure dependence. These results demonstrate that the emergence of interlayer magnetic ordering can be predicted from the microscopic interlayer exchange coupling, establishing a predictive framework for understanding and designing interlayer coupling phenomena in layered magnetic materials.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Can end-to-end learning from raw electronic structure explain magnetic anisotropy?
item.description: arXiv:2610.11742v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine-learning models trained directly on electronic spectra can predict spin--orbit-driven properties, yet models with comparable predictive accuracy may learn different electronic dependencies. We examine this problem using magnetic anisotropy in atomic-scale magnets and a validation strategy designed to assess the physical relevance of learned spectral relationships. We compare a bidirectional gated recurrent unit and a one-dimensional convolutional neural network, both trained to predict magnetic anisotropy energy (MAE) from spin- and orbital-resolved scalar-relativistic densities of states (SR-DOS). Despite comparable in-domain (ID) accuracy, the architectures learn only partly overlapping spectral dependencies. Shapley additive explanations identify spectral features shared between the two architectures that can be associated with plausible spin--orbit-coupling pathways consistent with second-order perturbation theory (PT2). Adding PT2-derived MAE contributions to the model inputs has little effect on ID performance but can improve transfer beyond the training domain, with gains differing between architectures. Controlled spectral perturbations further demonstrate that similar attribution patterns do not imply the same functional dependence of the predicted MAE on spectral weight. The contrasting responses provide a functional context for architecture-dependent out-of-domain transfer. End-to-end learning can identify candidate electronic signatures of magnetic anisotropy. Their credible microscopic interpretation, however, rests on convergent evidence from predictive performance, model comparison, physical theory, controlled spectral interventions, and evaluation under distribution shift.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Field-resolved hierarchy of superconducting energy gaps in PdTe
item.description: arXiv:2610.12075v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Resolving how multiple superconducting energy scales evolve under magnetic field is important for distinguishing multiband, anisotropic, and surface-sensitive superconducting responses. Here, we investigate the superconducting state of PdTe using low-temperature soft point-contact spectroscopy in a sealed $^3$He immersion environment. The resulting Andreev-reflection spectra reveal two characteristic superconducting energy scales near 0.5 and 1.1 meV that are not adequately described by a single-gap BTK model. Both energy scales are progressively suppressed upon warming toward the same superconducting transition temperature $T_c$. In contrast, their magnetic-field evolution reveals two distinct characteristic fields near 4.5 and 7.5 kG. The lower scale is associated with the loss of the zero-resistance superconducting state, whereas the higher-energy spectroscopic response persists to substantially larger fields. Independent field-dependent gap analysis yields suppression scales consistent with those identified from the zero-bias conductance. These results reveal a field-resolved hierarchy of superconducting energy scales in PdTe and indicate superconducting responses with distinct magnetic-field robustness.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] PXtal: Learning to Align Powder X-Ray Diffraction and Crystal Structures under Information Asymmetry across Modalities
item.description: arXiv:2610.10653v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scientific multimodal learning commonly assumes that paired views are comparably informative. Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) makes this mismatch explicit: compressing a three-dimensional crystal structure into a one-dimensional diffraction pattern loses information and makes the pattern harder to connect to the crystal structure that produced it. We introduce PXtal, a framework for learning aligned PXRD and crystal representations under this physically imposed information asymmetry. PXtal uses Unbalanced Optimal Transport (UOT) to adapt the cross-modal coupling and coupling-level generalized Kullback-Leibler (GKL) divergence to supervise the full transport plan. Across six test sets, including four zero-shot transfer sets, PXtal consistently outperforms the baseline models in PXRD-to-crystal candidate retrieval, with the largest gains when PXRD patterns have close but crystallographically distinct nonpaired neighbors, meaning similar input patterns associated with different crystals. The resulting crystal and PXRD encoders transfer more effectively to downstream materials and crystallographic tasks. These results identify information asymmetry as a general design problem in scientific multimodal learning: alignment objectives should reflect what each modality preserves.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Generalized Langevin equation and fluctuation-dissipation theorem for particle-bath systems in external oscillating fields
item.description: arXiv:1802.09848v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Generalized Langevin Equation (GLE) can be derived from a particle-bath Hamiltonian, in both classical and quantum dynamics, and provides a route to the (both Markovian and non-Markovian) fluctuation-dissipation theorem (FDT). All previous studies have focused either on particle-bath systems with time-independent external forces only, or on the simplified case where only the tagged particle is subject to the external time-dependent oscillatory field. Here we extend the GLE and the corresponding FDT for the more general case where both the tagged particle and the bath oscillators respond to an external oscillatory field. This is the example of a charged or polarisable particle immersed in a bath of other particles that are also charged or polarizable, under an external AC electric field. For this Hamiltonian, we find that the ensemble average of the stochastic force is not zero, but proportional to the AC field. The associated FDT reads as $\langle F_P(t)F_P(t')\rangle=mk_BT\nu(t-t')+(\gamma e)^2E(t)E(t')$, where $F_{p}$ is the random force, $\nu(t-t')$ is the friction memory function, and $\gamma$ is a numerical prefactor.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Experimental signature of transient symmetry breaking in a cavity superconductor
item.description: arXiv:2511.01339v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Transient states of matter far from equilibrium may exhibit physical properties beyond those allowed by the equilibrium-state crystalline symmetries. We explore ultrafast and direct electronic excitations of transient states in a cavity superconductor by using time-resolved terahertz-pump terahertz-probe spectroscopy. Our results show that the strong terahertz field can transiently modify the symmetries of the electronic subsystems via the injection of a transient supercurrent, leading to high-order nonlinear dynamical responses that are not compatible with the equilibrium-state symmetries, which evidences for transient symmetry breaking on the picosecond time scale. Our study also finds that the strong coupling of the superconductor to the designed microcavities enables the sensitive detection of the nonlinear responses associated to the transient symmetry breaking.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Pressure-induced Lifshitz and quantum phase transitions in electron-doped cuprate superconductor
item.description: arXiv:2512.11439v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We report the first observations of a pressure-induced Lifshitz transition coupled with a quantum phase transition in electron-doped cuprate superconductor Pr0.87LaCe0.13CuO4 (PLCCO), by combining high-pressure electrical resistance, Hall coefficient and synchrotron X-ray diffraction (XRD) measurements at low temperatures. Our low-temperature Hall coefficient measurements reveal that the Hall coefficient decreases continuously and reaches zero at about 10 GPa (critical pressure of Pc1). Upon further compression beyond Pc1, Hall coefficient unexpectedly changes its sign from negative to positive, signaling a reconstruction of the Fermi surface from electron-dominated to hole-dominated topology. Concurrently, the superconducting transition temperature (Tc) exhibits a monotonic suppression, vanishing completely at 17.6 GPa (critical pressure of Pc2), where the system enters a non-superconducting metallic state. Our low temperature XRD measurements unequivocally demonstrate the absence of any structural phase transition across Pc1 and Pc2. Therefore, the sign change in RH at Pc1 is associated with a Lifshitz transition, which is never found in the compressed bulk electron- or hole-doped cuprate superconductors. Moreover, the quantum phase transition observed at Pc2 contrasts sharply with known high-pressure behavior of hole-doped cuprates, uncovering a fundamental difference on how pressure tunes the ground states of electron- versus hole-doped systems. These findings provide crucial insights into the different pressure responses on the interplay among Fermi surface topology, electronic correlations, and superconductivity between these two kinds of cuprate superconductors.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Spin-orbit coupling effects in altermagnets: Interplay of weak spin and orbital ferromagnetism with relativistic splitting of electron states
item.description: arXiv:2605.01780v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The aim of the paper is to contribute to reaching a deeper understanding of the formation of relativistic effects in altermagnets. The focus of the paper is on the phenomena of weak ferromagnetism (WFM) and relativistic DFT calculations combined with the symmetry analysis on the basis of spin space groups. The consideration is performed on two different levels. On the first level, the atomistic magnetic structure of weak ferromagnetic state is calculated. Both spin and orbital atomic moments are taken into account. We study the dependence of the WFM moment on the strength of the SOC and obtain a peculiar nonmonotonous type of dependence. An interesting result is obtained in quasisymmetry (QS) calculation where only the component of the SOC collinear to the N\'eel vector is taken into account. In QS calculation the spin WFM is absent while the orbital WFM is present. This reveals a principal difference in the formation of the spin and orbital magnetic moments. On the second level, the study is focused on the properties of individual electron states. We introduce the notion of the magnetic structure of the electron state (MSES). It is shown how the collinear spin-MSESs of both metal and ligand atoms and compensated orbital-MSES of the ligand obtained in the nonrelativiatic calculation transform into complex noncollinear 3D MSESs of both spin and orbital nature. An important role in the formation of MSESs is played by the relativistic splitting of the accidental spin degeneracies at general {\bf k} points filling the volume of the Brillouin zone. The formation of the regions of avoided crossings in the relativistic band structure is related to the nonmonotonous behavior of the WFM moment. The importance of the metal-ligand hybridization in the formation of the AM properties is discussed. Most of the calculations are performed for MnTe.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Compositional and Magnetic Characterisation of Oblique Co and Fe Nanowire Structures Fabricated Using Focused Electron Beam Induced Deposition
item.description: arXiv:2605.14673v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Focused electron beam induced deposition (FEBID) is an additive manufacturing technique uniquely suited for fabricating functional 3D nanostructures for a range of applications, including spintronic devices. However, the variation of growth dynamics associated with lateral movement of the electron beam results in structures with non-uniform composition when fabricating intricate 3D geometries. Herein, we measure changes in atomic composition and corresponding changes in magnetic induction in 3D ferromagnetic nanostructures with overhanging elements, e.g. bridges or arches. To investigate the effects of electron beam lateral movement, we fabricated Co and Fe nanowire (NW) structures with growth angle relative to the optic axis varying from 0{\deg} to 90{\deg}. The (scanning) transmission electron microscopy techniques of electron energy loss spectroscopy and off-axis electron holography were performed to map the NW elemental composition and magnetic induction as a function of NW growth angle. Comparison of the results reveals a reduction in metal content with increased growth angle in FEBID NWs. The magnitude of metal content reduction can be tuned by controlling electron beam parameters, and ferromagnetic NWs with approximately equal metal content at growth angles from 0{\deg} to 60{\deg} were fabricated by using the lowest viable electron beam voltage and the highest viable beam current to reduce the interaction volume and increase the metal content, respectively.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Transforming Native Oxide into a Metallic Platinum--Niobium Alloy for Passivation of Superconducting Niobium Films
item.description: arXiv:2607.00429v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Dielectric losses at surfaces and interfaces remains a primary limitation to coherence in superconducting transmon qubits. Niobium (Nb), a widely used material in superconducting quantum circuits, readily forms native oxides under ambient conditions, leading to lossy dielectric interfaces that degrade device performance. Here, we demonstrate a novel fabrication strategy that chemically transforms the native dielectric oxide on Nb into a metallic Pt--Nb surface alloy through post-oxidation Pt deposition followed by thermal annealing, thereby stabilizing Nb surfaces against further oxidation, potentially including sidewall regions. High-purity Nb films were fabricated with bulk-like superconducting transition temperatures ($T_c = 9.30\pm0.10$~K). Spectroscopic and microscopic analyses confirm the conversion of the native oxide into a chemically stable, metallic alloy-dominated layer that suppresses subsequent oxide growth. Ab initio simulations elucidate the atomic-scale rearrangement and electronic structure evolution associated with Pt incorporation into native niobium oxide, providing insight into the mechanism underlying the oxide-to-metal transformation and stabilization of the alloyed surface.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Why Ammoniated Lithium Borohydrides Liquefy and Resolidify?
item.description: arXiv:2608.01266v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Ammonia (NH$_3$) absorption drives LiBH$_4\cdot x$NH$_3$ through a re-entrant ``solid--liquid--solid'' transition: LiBH$_4\cdot$NH$_3$ is a well-defined solid ammoniate, compositions near LiBH$_4\cdot 2$NH$_3$ are liquid-like or partially liquefied, whereas LiBH$_4\cdot 3$NH$_3$ returns to a more rigid non-liquid ammoniate state. However, the microscopic origin of this unintuitive response remains a long-lasting mystery. Here, we uncover its mechanism. Cross-database analysis identifies borohydrides as a particularly state-diverse and composition-responsive material family. Structure prediction and ab initio molecular simulations reveal that increasing NH$_3$ loading increases the direct Li--N coordination number while progressively decreasing BH$_4^-$-associated contacts in the local Li environment. Near $x \approx 2$, these contributions are most balanced among the simulated compositions, and the sampled Li--N/N$\cdots$B coordination landscape is broadest. Further ammoniation produces Li--N-dominant coordination and slower BH$_4^-$/NH$_3$ contact renewal, accompanying recovery of a more rigid ammoniate state. Pressure--composition isotherm, $^1$H and $^{11}$B nuclear magnetic resonance, and Raman measurements support this non-monotonic state evolution and associated BH$_4^-$/NH$_3$ reorganization. These findings transform ammonia-induced liquefaction from an empirical phase anomaly into a competition between native-network disruption, mixed-coordination frustration, and ligand-built network reconstruction, providing a framework for chemically switching between transport-favouring fluidity and stability-favouring rigidity in hydrogen-rich materials.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cond-mat updates on arXiv.org] Variational representation and estimates for the free energy of a quenched charged polymer model
item.description: arXiv:2502.18964v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Random walks with a disordered self-interaction potential may be used to model charged polymers. In this paper we consider a one-dimensional and directed version of the charged polymer model that was introduced by Derrida, Griffiths and Higgs. We prove new results for the associated quenched free energy, including a variational formula based on a quenched large deviation principle established by Birkner, Greven and den Hollander. We also take the occasion to (i) provide detailed proofs for state-of-the-art results pointing towards the existence of a freezing transition and (ii) proceed with minor corrections for two results previously obtained by the present author with Caravenna, den Hollander and P{\'e}tr{\'e}lis for the undirected model.
item.author: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs.AR updates on arXiv.org] RFChipAgent: Multi-Agentic AI Flow for Analog/RF Chip Design
item.description: arXiv:2610.10858v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Analog/RF circuits remain the critical interface between digital computation and the physical world, and emerging standards from Wi-Fi 7 to 6G place stringent demands on them, yet analog/RF design remains one of the most labor-intensive steps in chip development. We present RFChipAgent, a first-of-its-kind multi-agent flow of large language model (LLM) agents for end-to-end analog/RF circuit design automation, in which AI agents collaboratively orchestrate the complete design flow under human supervision. RFChipAgent is built around four technical pillars. First, a multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) subsystem with private per-document FAISS indexing extracts design knowledge from existing engineering documentation. Second, a topology agent drives topology selection, and a schematic and testbench agent automates circuit and testbench assembly. Third, a closed-loop hybrid circuit-sizing engine combines Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) and CMA-ES optimization, evaluating every candidate in a simulator-in-the-loop framework. Fourth, a trust-scored simulation database accumulates verified performance data and builds an adaptive optimization model that informs subsequent trials. We validate RFChipAgent on a family of GF22FDSOI 60 GHz wideband mm-wave low-noise amplifier (LNA) topologies, demonstrating automated topology generation, specification-driven design-space exploration, and simulator-guided optimization. Experimental results show substantial reductions in design effort while maintaining signoff-quality verification. This work establishes a foundation for LLM-driven multi-agent electronic design automation (EDA) for analog/RF circuits.
item.author: cs.AR updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs.AR updates on arXiv.org] Bridging the Last Mile of Circuit Design: PostEDA-Bench, a Hierarchical Benchmark for PPA Convergence and DRC Fixing
item.description: arXiv:2605.06936v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly applied to the "last mile" of Electronic Design Automation (EDA): repairing residual sign-off Design Rule Check (DRC) violations and converging Power-Performance-Area (PPA) targets after tool runs. Existing EDA-LLM benchmarks, however, omit DRC fixing entirely and rely on flat hierarchies tied to a single toolchain. We introduce PostEDA-Bench, a hierarchical benchmark with 145 tasks across DRC-Essential, DRC-Reasoning, PPA-Mono, and PPA-Multi, supported by EDA toolchains with machine-checkable evaluation. Across eight commercial and open-source LLMs under multiple agent scaffolds, we find that agents handle synthetic DRC-Essential and single-objective PPA-Mono reasonably well but degrade sharply on the more practical DRC-Reasoning, where the best success rate is 36.66%, and PPA-Multi, where the best success rate is 20.00%; vision augmentation consistently enhances DRC-Bench; and trade-off reasoning, rather than knob knowledge, is the dominant PPA-Multi bottleneck.
